bull.b: Strong cloud growth, expanding contracted backlog, and net revenue retention above 120% indicate durable customer adoption and expansion. These recurring indicators support predictable revenue compounding, improve visibility, and reinforce Atlassian’s position across collaborative enterprise workflows.

Atlassian converts revenue into substantial operating and free cash flow despite reported net losses. This cash generation provides internal funding for product development, AI investment, and customer growth while improving resilience and reducing reliance on external financing over the next several quarters.

Broad enterprise Rovo adoption and rapidly increasing usage strengthen Atlassian’s strategic role in large organizations. AI features embedded in established workflows can deepen engagement, support cross-selling, and create a durable platform advantage as customers expand automation across teams.

bear.b: Although losses narrowed, persistent negative GAAP earnings show that Atlassian has not yet demonstrated consistent accounting profitability. Continued spending and volatile operating results could limit flexibility and make durable earnings conversion dependent on future cost discipline and revenue scale.

bear.t: Lower FY27 Growth and Margin Guidance
bear.b: Management’s outlook implies a meaningful moderation from FY26’s 23% subscription ARR growth and Q4’s 12% GAAP operating margin. The lower guide suggests growth and profitability may remain sensitive to investment needs, lapping effects, and broader uncertainty during the coming year.

Leverage has improved substantially but remains meaningful relative to equity, while negative ROE reflects the company’s continuing accounting losses. This reduces balance-sheet flexibility compared with a debt-light software model and could constrain capital allocation if profitability improvement takes longer.
